rules_evaluated.evidence: learn-from-the-test.md:101 — "Come to Module 6 without the packaged session and you'll have one session to read where the exercise needs two. Your call." Deviates from the compendium's literal "scrambling for Y" phrasing but passes on substance: student-as-subject, choice preserved ("Your call"), and the cost named (one session vs. the two the exercise needs) comes from the exercise's own structure, not room comparison (`grep -c 'while the room is already' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md` -> 0). None of the three named failure modes fire: no M6 mechanics explained beyond the session count, no head-start prompt, no unearned vocabulary. Noted as a todo for phrasing tightness, not filed as REVISE.

todos.note: M4->M5 offers no body-prose rescue callout for a thin/missing M4 send-off (only a trainer push-back), while M5->M6 does carry one for the structurally similar risk of a thin/missing M5 send-off. §6 is permissive (MAY), so this is not a gate, but the asymmetry is worth a maintainer look for consistency.

learn-from-the-test.md:101's stakes line ("you'll have one session to read where the exercise needs two") departs from the compendium's canonical "scrambling for Y while the exercise is already Z" phrasing. It passes the substantive test (subject, choice, exercise-clock cost) so it is not a REVISE, but tightening it toward the canonical shape would remove the judgement call for future judges.
